text: Manchester United are eighteenth. In the relegation zone.
Eight points from ten games. Eight league games without a win.
Start on the pitch. Carrick's four-two-three-one becomes a three-one-six with the ball.
Six men ahead of it, one man holding. Lose it, and there's a canyon between the press and the back four.
Against Villa, two-nil down inside four minutes. Full-backs high, two centre-backs left alone.
Twenty-six shots at home, and still three expected goals conceded.
Thirty conceded this season. More than any team in Europe's top five leagues.
Then look upstairs. The Glazers bought this club with borrowed money in 2005. Twenty years on, the club is still paying for it.
Ratcliffe runs the football, owns under a third, and the fans are turning on both.
Sunday's banner: we don't want a new stadium. We want the owners out.
It isn't one coach. It's the shape on the pitch, and the structure above it.
